note: 对官方抓包定义的本地改写：只改 description 与 parameters 的约束，不改工具名、不改 required 集合、不改 type、不改 properties 的键集合。

edit.description:
Replace exact text inside one existing file.

Use when: you have read a file and need to change part of it.
Don't use for: creating or replacing a whole file (write), or one change across several files (patch).

- oldString must match exactly once unless replaceAll is true; add surrounding lines to disambiguate.
- Copy text from the file itself, never from read output: strip the `NNN: ` line prefix.
- Matching retries ignoring curly quotes, en/em dashes and trailing whitespace, then fails when nothing matches.
- Line endings are preserved; to rewrite them, make oldString and newString differ only in `\r`.
- newString must differ from oldString; pass "" to delete the matched text.

path.description: File to edit. Relative paths resolve against the session working directory.

oldString.description: Exact text to find. Must match the file as it is on disk; include neighbouring lines when it is ambiguous.

newString.description: Replacement text; must differ from oldString. Empty string deletes the match.

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring exactly one match. Default: false.

execute.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script and compose tool calls.

Use when: one step needs many tool calls, concurrency, or the output of one call feeding the next.
Don't use for: a single command (shell) or a single file read or write (read/write).

- Only tools in this Code Mode catalog, or ones returned by `search`, are callable inside `{ code }`.
- Call them as `tools.ns["tool-name"]({...})`; keep the exact path, never rename or normalize it.
- `fetch` does HTTP; imports, filesystem access and timers do not exist.
- End with `return <value>`: the last top-level expression becomes the result.
- Await every call that matters; run independent calls with `Promise.allSettled`.

code.description: JavaScript body of the script. Top-level await is allowed; the last evaluated expression becomes the result.

glob.description:
Find files by path glob and return the matching paths.

Use when: you know part of a name or path and need the files it matches.
Don't use for: text inside files (grep) or reading contents (read).

- `**/*.ts` matches at any depth; a bare `*.ts` also searches the whole tree.
- `path` picks the root (default: working directory); `hidden` includes dotfiles; `limit` caps results (default 100).

pattern.description: Glob pattern such as `**/*.ts` or `src/**/*.tsx`; it matches file paths, not directories.

path.description: Directory to search under. Default: the session working directory.

hidden.description: Include dotfiles and hidden directories. Default: false.

limit.description: Maximum number of paths returned. Default: 100.

grep.description:
Search file contents by regex or literal text; returns matching lines.

Use when: you need where a symbol, string or pattern occurs in code.
Don't use for: finding files by name (glob) or reading a whole file (read).

- `pattern` is a ripgrep regex unless `literal` is true.
- Narrow with `path` (file or dir) and `include` (glob); `caseSensitive` default true.
- `limit` caps returned matches (default 100).

pattern.description: Ripgrep regular expression, or plain text when literal is true. Must be non-empty.

path.description: File or directory to search. Default: the session working directory.

include.description: Glob filter on file names, e.g. `*.js` or `*.{ts,tsx}`. Optional.

literal.description: Treat pattern as plain text instead of a regex. Default: false.

question.description:
Ask the user to pick an option or supply a missing value; the turn waits for the answer.

Use when: a decision belongs to the user, or a required input cannot be inferred.
Don't use for: anything you can check in the repo or in the tools, or that has a safe default.

- Give concrete options; a free-form "type your own answer" choice is added automatically.
- Put the recommended option first and end its label with "(Recommended)".
- `multiple: true` lets the user pick several options.
- `header` is at most 30 characters; each `label` is 1-5 words.

questions.description: Questions to ask in this turn; at least one.

read.description:
Read a file or directory; text lines come back numbered from 1.

Use when: you need the exact text of a file or a directory listing.
Don't use for: changing files (edit/write), finding files (glob) or searching text (grep).

- `offset` is the 1-based first line, `limit` the maximum lines; page long files instead of reading all.
- Directory entries come back one per line.
- Images and PDFs are returned to the model directly.
- To reuse text in edit, strip the `NNN: ` prefix first.

offset.description: 1-based index of the first line or directory entry to return. Default: 1.

limit.description: Maximum lines or directory entries returned, capped at 2000. Default: 2000.

shell.description:
Run a shell command and return its stdout and stderr.

Use when: you need git, build, test or OS commands in the workspace.
Don't use for: file reads, writes or edits (read/write/edit), searching (glob/grep), or scripting tool calls (execute).

- One fresh shell per call: pass `workdir` instead of chaining `cd`.
- Long output is truncated in the reply while the full text is saved to a file.
- `timeout` is milliseconds (default 120000); a `background` job returns at once and notifies you.

command.description: Command line to run. Quoting and interpolation follow the shell in use.

workdir.description: Directory to run in. Default: the session working directory.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds; 0 disables it. Default: 120000 for foreground calls.

background.description: Run detached and return immediately; you are notified on completion. Default: false.

skill.description:
Load a skill's full instructions into this conversation.

Use when: the task matches a skill in the available skills list, or the user names one.
Don't use for: one-step work the current tools already cover.

- `id` must be the exact skill name from the list; a near miss loads nothing.
- Follow the loaded instructions before acting on the task.

id.description: Exact skill id from the available skills list.

subagent.description:
Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent that works in its own context.

Use when: a chunk of work is independent and would flood this conversation with detail.
Don't use for: one or two local calls, or fan-out over many items (use execute).

- New children start with a fresh context: restate every fact they cannot infer.
- `sessionID` resumes that child's earlier conversation; omitting it starts a new one.
- `background: true` returns at once and notifies you later; use it only for independent work.
- The child returns its result, not its tool transcript; relay what matters to the user.

Agents: `explore` (fast read-only codebase search), `general` (multi-step work).

agent.description: Agent to run: `explore` for fast read-only search, `general` for multi-step work.

description.description: Short 3-5 word label shown to the user.

prompt.description: Complete self-contained task for the child, including all context it needs.

background.description: Run in the background and return immediately; you are notified on completion. Default: false.

sessionID.description: Resume this child's conversation (id starts with `ses`). Omit to start a new one.

model.description: Leave unset unless the user asks for a specific model; format `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant`.

webfetch.description:
Fetch one HTTP(S) URL and return its content as text, markdown or HTML.

Use when: you already have the URL and need the page itself.
Don't use for: discovering sources or current facts (websearch).

- Read-only: it makes no state changes.
- `format` defaults to markdown; `timeout` is seconds, greater than 0 and at most 120.
- Large pages return a preview; the full text is kept in managed storage.

url.description: Absolute http:// or https:// URL to fetch.

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds, greater than 0 and at most 120.

websearch.description:
Search the web and return an answer summary with source links.

Use when: the answer depends on current events, releases or docs newer than the model cutoff.
Don't use for: pages you already have a URL for (webfetch) or code in this repo (grep).

- The current year is 2026; name it when searching recent events.
- Read a hit in full with webfetch.

query.description: Search query, ideally carrying the product, version or year that pins the result.

write.description:
Create or overwrite a whole file, creating parent directories as needed.

Use when: writing a new file or replacing one entirely.
Don't use for: partial changes (edit) or multi-file diffs (patch).

- Content is written verbatim; no trailing newline is added.
- Overwrites silently, with no backup.

path.description: File to write. Relative paths resolve against the session working directory.

content.description: Full file contents, UTF-8, written exactly as given.

patch.description:
Apply a multi-file diff in a stripped-down patch format.

Use when: one change spans several files, or whole-file writes would fight exact text matching.
Don't use for: a single small edit (edit) or creating one file (write).

The patch language is a file-oriented diff. One envelope, then one or more file sections:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: <path>
+<line of initial content>
*** Update File: <path>
*** Move to: <new path>
@@ <anchor line>
-<removed line>
+<added line>
*** Delete File: <path>
*** End Patch

- Start with `*** Begin Patch` and end with `*** End Patch`; every section needs its `***` header.
- Add and update lines start with `+`, removed lines with `-`; `*** Move to:` follows its `*** Update File:`.
- `@@ <anchor>` selects where the hunk applies inside the file.

patchText.description: Complete patch: the Begin/End envelope plus one or more Add/Update/Delete sections.
